product.name: LocalCloud
product.productionBoundary: LocalCloud emulates bounded local development workflows. Validate application behavior against real Google Cloud before production deployment.

runtimeImage.limitation: The repository agrees across the reviewed runtime launcher and CLI, but the mutable latest tag has no qualified assembled-image digest.

operator.manualDockerCommand:
docker volume create localcloud-data

docker run -d --name localcloud \
  -p 127.0.0.1:5380-5405:5380-5405 \
  -m 4g \
  -v localcloud-data:/var/lib/localcloud \
  jaysen2apache/localcloud:latest

supportedHosts: Linux with glibc 2.35+ on arm64 or amd64
cli.integrity: The installer verifies SHA-256 checksums, exact archive members, and the executable semantic version. Release automation separately publishes Sigstore bundles; install.sh does not verify them.
cli.releaseBoundary: CLI 0.1.5 behavior is documented from the current sibling source snapshot. Source digests identify working-tree changes not captured by cliRevision. Use localcloud --version to confirm the installed release.

A projects mapping whose entries each contain service seed data.

limitations: Firestore has no enabled seed registrar.
LOCALCLOUD_TERRAFORM_MODE=true skips seeding.
Volatile mode is bounded to registered volatile seed targets; verify the selected service before relying on restart behavior.

terraform.credentialRequirement: A syntactically valid fake service-account JSON file; /dev/null is not sufficient for provider v7.

networkModes.description: Use generated custom endpoints for resources whose provider clients honor them.
requirements: eval generated values from /env?format=terraform or localcloud env --format terraform

networkModes.description: Use LocalCloud DNS/HTTP/HTTPS routing for clients that ignore custom endpoints.

BigQuery ignores its custom endpoint and requires transparent routing.
Resource support is bounded to maintained qualification evidence.
A service-error/crash event method exists but no main-source caller was found.
Disabling telemetry emits a telemetry_disabled event before suppression.

outboundBehaviors.control: CLI/runtime configuration; verify the release used

limitations: Core operation can continue offline after the image is present only when outbound features are disabled or unused; do not describe the product as categorically offline.

licensing.summary: The proprietary Public Preview License permits individuals and organizations, including for-profit companies, to use LocalCloud free of charge for internal development, testing, CI, evaluation, and internal pilots.
licensing.permittedUse: Non-production personal, academic, nonprofit, and company use for internal development, debugging, testing, quality assurance, ongoing CI and delivery automation, evaluation, proofs of concept, and internal pilots.
excludedUse: reselling LocalCloud or providing it as a hosted or managed service
modification except where applicable law requires permission

technicalEnforcement.developmentBuild: Enforcement may be disabled and technical Pro access granted.
technicalEnforcement.enforcedBuild: Public-preview release images explicitly disable key enforcement; a separately enforced build requires LOCALCLOUD_API_KEY and terminates startup when validation fails.
technicalEnforcement.serviceTiers: localcloud.defaults.yaml minTier controls technical service availability when tier enforcement is active but does not define pricing plans or grant legal permission.

limitations: Technical tier availability does not grant legal permission.
The proprietary preview grant excludes production use, hosted or managed service use, redistribution, sublicensing, and modification.
Each Preview Release keeps its granted terms even if future releases use different terms.
Conflicting Apache-2.0 package or OCI metadata does not override the governing root LICENSE.

services.name: Cloud Storage

persistence.restartBehavior: Survives process and container restart while the LocalCloud volume is retained
recoveryLimitations: No production durability or replication semantics.

limitations: [partial] Bucket policy APIs use gateway 5380/TLS 5381. Object authorization is enforced at both direct listeners and the gateway when IAM mode requires it.
[partial] gcp-live uses caller-token Google permission checks with no fallback. Real-Google and object-conditional grant qualification remain pending; unsupported remote grants fail closed.
[partial] Open mode deliberately permits known-bucket access; project listing uses authoritative ownership and is not an open-mode tenant security boundary.
[partial] Notification delivery uses precreated local Pub/Sub topics. Persisted messages retry after failure/restart; ordering and transactional object/outbox crash atomicity are not promised.

[unsupported] Filesystem-backed buckets do not support versioning or OBJECT_ARCHIVE notifications. Finalize, metadata-update and delete delivery are live-container qualified; versioning is a separate development gap, not production-only.

[partial] HMAC supports local project-ID-scoped service-account identities. Project-number aliases and default-compute identities are not resolved; real-Google gcp-live impersonation is not qualified. Secrets are excluded from project YAML exports; encrypted key state is retained in full filesystem snapshots.
[prod_only] Object lifecycle scheduling, retention policies and retention enforcement are production-only and excluded from developer completeness.
[unsupported] Managed-folder APIs are not implemented.

[partial] Path-style HMAC XML requests accept localhost and loopback IPs with discovered Docker ports. Virtual-host requests use the configured public hostname (localhost); signed Host headers must not be rewritten after signing.

[partial] Local live-container HTTP qualification includes multipart uploads, admin caller propagation, strict signed IAM, notification recovery and reset. These fixes require a rebuilt image; trusted release-image and full LocalCloud TLS qualification remain pending.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog and remains subject to license-tier gates.

limitations: Production governance and automatic lifecycle scheduling are outside the developer support contract by product decision.

services.name: Firestore

persistence.restartBehavior: Documents do not have an audited persisted data directory in the assembled container
recoveryLimitations: Treat restart persistence as unsupported.

limitations: Firestore is not currently supported by LocalCloud. References and emulator configurations are maintained for future implementation.

Native REST create/query and document-value recovery after clean restart passed on an isolated existing local image. Root collection browsing uses GET /documents, which returned 404; ListCollectionIds succeeded with emulator admin authentication.

Global reset enumerates Console-registered projects. Firestore namespaces created only through the native API under unregistered projects are outside that enumeration. Reset clears the default database and this project's named databases recorded in the latest checkpoint; named databases created since that checkpoint cannot be discovered through the current public emulator API.

Firestore reset deleted_count counts cleared database namespaces, not deleted documents. Resetting a disabled backend temporarily starts and imports it without changing configured enablement, then requires a confirmed stop and a new checkpoint generation before success. The disabled-reset regression passed JAR-overlay batch7; final exact-image qualification remains pending.
The isolated restart restored document content but changed createTime/updateTime; timestamp and precondition fidelity need recovery fixes and native SDK tests.

Composite-index enforcement, transaction concurrency, listeners and transforms require exact-artifact qualification. Security Rules evaluation and Firestore-trigger delivery remain unqualified local capabilities.

services.name: Spanner

persistence.backingStore: LevelDB rows plus JSON metadata at /var/lib/localcloud/spanner-data
persistence.restartBehavior: Ordinary container stop/start retains state; a mounted /var/lib/localcloud volume is required to retain state across container removal or replacement
recoveryLimitations: Rows use LevelDB and metadata uses JSON files.
Known corruption/recovery risk; internal safety snapshots are not Cloud Spanner Backup API.

limitations: Extended Spanner emulator image supports 140 features (1 partial [schema.queues], 8 accepted-no-op, 9 production-only exclusions, 0 unsupported out of 158 feature records). Public-endpoint client matrix is 100% verified against native builds and packaged Docker image with Python (3.71.0), Go (1.95.1), Node.js (9.0.0), Java (6.123.0), JDBC (2.45.0), and PGAdapter (0.55.3 with pgJDBC and psql).

Database roles and fine-grained access control (FGAC) are enforced for sessions created with a creator_role. Unauthenticated emulator connections bypass IAM principal identity checks; stored IAM policies do not enforce network identity.
Change streams require ExecuteStreamingSql; unary ExecuteSql rejects change-stream queries. With --data_dir, stream definitions, records, partition history, and resume tokens survive restarts.
Backups require --data_dir; each backup is a full database copy. Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) are not implemented (data is plaintext).

Production-only infrastructure exclusions (Google TrueTime hardware clock, multi-region Paxos quorum switching, physical split points and tablet distribution, physical cross-region migration, multi-tenant compute slicing) do not apply to local development.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog and remains subject to license-tier gates.

operations.label: Native SQL, read, and streaming read
limitations: Native ExecuteSql and ExecuteStreamingSql in both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects. StreamingRead and ExecuteStreamingSql stream whole rows with resume tokens at row boundaries. Unary ExecuteSql intentionally retains the emulator's rejection of change-stream queries. Full-text search (TOKENIZE_*, SEARCH, SNIPPET, SCORE), vector search (APPROX_* / ScaNN), and 13 graph algorithms (PageRank, ShortestPath, etc.) compute locally.

operations.label: Sessions, transactions, and batch DML
limitations: Sessions (including batch create and multiplexed), read-write, read-only and single-use transactions. SERIALIZABLE (default) and REPEATABLE_READ isolation. Conflicts follow wound-wait lock waits (--lock_wait_timeout_ms). Exclusive locks via SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and LOCK_SCANNED_RANGES=exclusive. Commit timestamps (PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP) and commit stats (mutation count). Deadlock aborts exactly one transaction. Unique indexes are re-checked at commit.

operations.label: Partition query/read and batch write
limitations: PartitionRead, PartitionQuery, partitioned DML (including parameterized PostgreSQL statements), and BatchWrite are supported.

operations.label: Instance, configuration, and instance-partition administration
limitations: Instance and instance-partition administration, custom instance configurations, and MoveInstance (metadata). List operations and instances support AIP-160 filter expressions.

operations.label: Database administration and DDL
limitations: Database creation, DDL execution for both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL, drop protection (UpdateDatabase), ListDatabaseOperations, split points (AddSplitPoints persisted to SPANNER_SYS.USER_SPLIT_POINTS), and fine-grained access control database roles (CREATE/DROP ROLE, GRANT/REVOKE, ListDatabaseRoles).

operations.label: Instance and database IAM policies
limitations: IAM policies are stored durably in LevelDB and returned through native endpoints with etags guarded. Fine-grained access control (FGAC) is enforced for sessions created with a creator_role on queries, DML, reads, mutations, and change stream reads. Unauthenticated emulator connections bypass network IAM.

operations.label: Backup, copy, restore, and backup schedules
limitations: With --data_dir, CreateBackup, CopyBackup, GetBackup, ListBackups (with AIP-160 filter precedence), UpdateBackup, DeleteBackup, RestoreDatabase, and ListBackupOperations are supported. version_time backups and full/incremental backup schedules persist cursors across restarts.

operations.label: Long-running operation lifecycle
limitations: Native long-running operations lifecycle across instance, database, backup, copy, and restore calls, with AIP-160 filter support.

services.name: BigQuery

persistence.restartBehavior: Survives restart with the LocalCloud volume
recoveryLimitations: Assembled dependency identity remains release-unverified.

limitations: 1,065 canonical capabilities are implemented across development and production parity (945/996 GoogleSQL capabilities in the census). GoogleSQL Analyzer (pinned ZetaSQL 2026.9.2) provides exact semantic resolution and fail-closed validation with 0 silent wrong results.

Full 76-digit BIGNUMERIC, NUMERIC(38,9), and GEOGRAPHY functions (ST_BOUNDINGBOX, ST_INTERSECTSBOX, ST_CLUSTERDBSCAN, ST_ASGEOJSON, etc.) are implemented. Procedural SQL (DECLARE, SET, IF/WHILE/LOOP, BEGIN/EXCEPTION, EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, CALL) and stored procedures are fully supported.
Row-level security on all read surfaces, data masking (Data Policy API v1), policy tags, and IAM Conditions evaluated with Google's CEL runtime (cel-expr-python) are enforced.
Time travel (FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF) and table clones with time travel are supported. BQML models (tabular, time-series, and local GenAI) and exact SEARCH / VECTOR_SEARCH are supported.

Remaining partial gaps across 11 canonical rows include policy tags on nested RECORD fields, TRANSFORM for select advanced model types, ingestion-time _PARTITIONTIME pseudocolumns, specialized S2 geometry snapping/union edge cases, and cross-architecture Spark profile attestation.

Production-only infrastructure exclusions (Google-managed distributed slot reservations, petabyte-scale multi-region durability, cross-region replication, continuous Pub/Sub streaming at petabyte scale) do not apply to local development.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog and remains subject to license-tier gates.

services.name: Cloud Tasks

persistence.restartBehavior: Queues, task bodies, and task state are reloaded after restart while the LocalCloud volume is retained
recoveryLimitations: Persistence does not recreate external HTTP side effects or provide production delivery, retry, ordering, or disaster-recovery guarantees.

limitations: OAuth/OIDC token minting, App Engine delivery, queue routing/header overrides and logging sampling are rejected as unsupported rather than silently stored.

No FIFO, exactly-once, dead-letter queue, transactional cancellation, adaptive Google throttling or production throughput guarantees. Removed task IDs have no Google-style deduplication tombstone. Unlimited retry settings have no automatic task-retention expiry.

HTTP attempt deadlines are durations from 15 to 1800 seconds (default 600). Failed attempts use configured fractional backoff; finite attempt and duration bounds must both be exhausted. A zero duration leaves only the attempt limit; -1 attempts is unlimited.

Local activity retains completed attempt metadata for seven days, with no request URL, headers, payload or response body archive. Interrupted or unpersisted outcomes may remain unknown. Successful/terminal tasks leave the active queue; absence alone is not success.

Pending and interrupted in-flight tasks recover after restart with possible redelivery. Pause, purge and deletion do not cancel requests already in flight. Never replay an ambiguous create or run request automatically.

BASIC omits payload and headers; FULL requires cloudtasks.tasks.fullView in enforcing IAM modes. Queue/task operations evaluate stored allow policies in strict and gcp-live modes; open/permissive modes do not enforce them.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog and remains subject to license-tier gates.

operations.label: queues.create/get/list/update/pause/resume/purge/delete
limitations: REST and gRPC share authorized, project/location-scoped queue lifecycle and dispatch settings. Console configuration uses an etag precondition; native service parity remains partial.

operations.label: tasks.create/get/list/delete/run
limitations: Durable task creation, BASIC/FULL inspection, pagination and immediate manual dispatch. Automatic dispatch honors queue rate/concurrency and fractional retry settings; retained local attempt records establish observed HTTP outcomes.

services.name: Cloud Scheduler

persistence.restartBehavior: Audited metadata survives restart while the LocalCloud volume is retained
recoveryLimitations: External runtime/data-plane side effects, if any, have separate lifecycle and recovery limits.

limitations: Five-field UNIX cron uses the installed cron-utils parser and Java IANA zones. Preview and dispatch share that parser. Tested cases include DST gaps/overlaps, leap dates, monthly day 31 and inclusive day-of-month/day-of-week semantics; this does not qualify every cron expression or future timezone database revision.
HTTP and Pub/Sub delivery are implemented. App Engine and OAuth/OIDC configurations are rejected before saving; Google-trusted credentials and managed App Engine execution are unavailable.

Queued runs and retries survive restart. An attempt interrupted while RUNNING becomes UNKNOWN and is not replayed because the target may already have received it. Manual runs can overlap; automatic schedules skip occurrences while an earlier automatic run or retry chain is active. Missed downtime occurrences are not backfilled.

Retry count is limited to 0–5, doublings to 0–16, and backoff to 0–86400 seconds. Fractional and explicit zero durations are retained. Retry duration starts with the first actual attempt; when both count and duration are configured both limits must be exhausted. HTTP deadlines are 15–1800 seconds; Pub/Sub ignores attemptDeadline.

Full project/location/job names scope jobs and history. Google-shaped endpoints retain configured gateway IAM enforcement; legacy browse/mutate endpoints retain the existing administrative bypass. Stored IAM policies do not establish per-job enforcement.

History returns at most 100 attempts for an exact owned job and optional since time. The Console loads all job pages before local filtering, then displays 25 jobs per page. Location names are namespaces, not residency guarantees.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog and remains subject to license-tier gates.

operations.label: jobs.create/list/get/update/delete/pause/resume/run
limitations: Shared REST, gRPC and admin lifecycle validates before persistence and schedules real HTTP/Pub/Sub delivery. Full job readback, masked updates, runtime cron preview, exact-owner history, durable queued retries and HTTP deadlines are verified. App Engine, OAuth and OIDC configurations are explicitly rejected; no credentials are fabricated.

services.name: Cloud SQL

persistence.backingStore: PostgreSQL/MySQL data directories plus PostgreSQL metadata under /var/lib/localcloud
persistence.restartBehavior: Data survives restart with the LocalCloud volume when Cloud SQL is enabled
recoveryLimitations: Backups and managed recovery are not emulated.
Assembled image currently disables Cloud SQL despite registry default-on.

limitations: PostgreSQL and shared on-demand MySQL 8.4 data planes exist; MySQL logical schemas and wire users are isolated per project/instance, not separate servers.

Only PostgreSQL/MySQL databaseVersion identifiers are accepted. Version labels map to the installed shared engines; they do not provision a separate engine version per instance. Per-instance databaseFlags are rejected and the flags catalog is empty; tier, disk, IP, backup and maintenance settings remain descriptive metadata. PATCH preserves omitted settings.

New databases apply native charset/collation and store native readback values. PostgreSQL encoding/collation cannot change in place; migrate data into a new database. MySQL ALTER DATABASE changes defaults, not existing column encodings. Older mismatched databases and missing user passwords require explicit repair or migration. New PostgreSQL clusters initialize with UTF8 encoding and C locale; existing clusters are preserved.

Required native work fails when the data plane is unavailable. Schema discovery returns per-database errors, shown in the Console. Creation reserves metadata before native provisioning and compensates newly created resources on failure.

SSL certificate endpoints use development certificate material. Public certificate inventory is persisted in PostgreSQL and deleted with its instance, with metadata derived from the actual certificate. Native TLS is not qualified.
backupRuns are emulated in PostgreSQL metadata; instances.restoreBackup and preCheckMajorVersionUpgrade are supported in instance administration.
Local read-replica lifecycle and PSC configuration are software gaps. Real managed regional replication and Google PSC transport are production-only.

Microsoft Entra ID, SSRS leases, external physical sync, blue-green deployments, cross-region failovers, and online disk shrink are production-only enterprise/infrastructure capabilities excluded from local development.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog and remains subject to license-tier gates.
